channel.title: Inkisle Journal
channel.description: The making of Inkisle, one post a day: design decisions, prototypes, mistakes and numbers.

item.title: Ink that spreads: the small effects that say what just happened
item.description: In Inkisle a captured island leaves a bloom of ink, a comeback shows a banner, and the last enemy island lights up. What each effect is for, how long it lasts, and how the first-run finger hint works.

item.title: A ten-second intro in three versions: sky, sea and land
item.description: Inkisle opens with a ten-second intro that comes in three versions. How the three share one ending, why a shuffled bag decides which one you see, when it shortens to three seconds, and what happens with reduce-motion turned on.

item.title: Sending from several islands at once: three rewrites of one control
item.description: Attacking one island from several of yours was the hardest control in Inkisle. The first drag-based version, the tap-to-select fix and the swipe-to-select version, and what each one taught us.

item.title: Tuning difficulty with bots: five stages that were wrong
item.description: We played every stage with simple bots for 40 seeds each and found stages that were impossible, too short or too hard. The five changes, the win rates before and after, and why bots are not people.

item.title: A playable prototype in a day
item.description: Sixteen stages, two seas and one HTML file of about 95 KB with no outside requests. How the prototype is built, what we tested in a headless browser, and what we could not test.

item.title: Art direction: three mockups, one pick
item.description: We asked for the same battle screen from our design assistant (two directions) and from GPT. What each returned, what went wrong with the outside mockup, and why minimal vector won.

item.title: Naming the game: how we ended up with Inkisle
item.description: Ten English name candidates, five finalists, a store and domain check, and why Inkisle won. Including the weak spots we know about and the checks we have not done.

item.title: The rules on one page: islands, troops, capture
item.description: Inkisle's whole rule set on one page: how islands produce troops, how fleets fly, how capture is calculated, and how a match ends. Starting values, before testing.

item.title: Four game ideas, one core: why we chose island conquest
item.description: We drafted four concepts for our next game. All four shared one core, sending troops between nodes. Here is why we kept the core, dropped the story and put it on the sea.
